decisions.executionNote: Raise and advance the right gripper toward the mouse, gradually pitching down while preserving the starting elbow-up branch.
Continue a high approach over the mouse, rotating the right gripper toward a downward grasp; left arm remains parked.
Lower the open right gripper over the mouse and finish the downward orientation; grasp depth will be checked in the wrist view.
Make a small wrist-image alignment correction around the mouse body, then close the right gripper. Retention is not yet established.
The mouse appears ahead of the closed jaws. Reopen and advance slightly to bracket its body before attempting another grasp.
Keep the mouse grasp closed, lift clear of the table, and begin a short transfer toward the pad; check that it follows the gripper.
Mouse remained on the table. Reopen and recenter the grasp leftward and slightly forward, at a lower depth.
Center the mouse between the jaws with a small rightward and downward correction, then close and settle before a lift test.
Lift the newly bracketed mouse and translate toward the pad with the jaws kept closed; inspect for retained motion.
The mouse follows the gripper. Carry it over the center of the pad and lower gently while keeping the grasp closed.
Release the mouse onto the pad and withdraw the right gripper. Raise the left arm to prepare a two-sided keyboard push without crossing workspaces.
Move both grippers to their respective sides in front of the keyboard, staying above the surface and leaving the released mouse behind.
Close both grippers into pushing contacts and lower symmetrically in front of the keyboard, without advancing into it yet.
Use both closed grippers to push the keyboard forward toward the outlined frame, with a small rightward alignment component.
Continue the balanced keyboard push to align its center with the frame; keep the left contact on the left side of the workspace.
Finish the small keyboard alignment, then open and withdraw both grippers. Begin moving the left arm toward the figurine while the right returns toward rest.
Approach the cactus figurine from above with the left gripper; return the right arm to its original workspace pose. Keyboard and mouse appear aligned with their targets.
Fine-align the open left gripper over the figurine's lower stem, using a more downward approach and modest descent.
The figurine tipped onto its side. Reposition the open left gripper over its pot for a lower recovery grasp rather than continuing the stem approach.
Lift clear before correcting the pot alignment forward and rightward, then descend with open jaws to avoid pushing it along the table.
Make a small backward and lower correction to bracket the tipped pot, close the left jaws, and begin a short retention test.
The pot is not retained. Reopen, lift clear, and recenter substantially left and forward using the wrist view before another grasp.
Replan from the interrupted pose: withdraw from the drawer face and use a shallower wrist angle to reach the pot without the wrist housing contacting the drawer.
The pot is behind the finger contact line. Move the open left jaws backward and slightly right and lower to bracket it, keeping clear of the drawer.
Center the pot laterally between the left jaws, close at the current contact height, and make a small lift to test retention.
The pot slipped rather than lifting. Reopen and make a deeper, centered grasp below its upper surface, then close without translating.
Lift the bracketed pot with the jaws closed and start toward the stand. Confirm the figurine is retained before attempting to right it.
The figurine stayed on the table. Return with open jaws to the pot and approach lower, since the prior contacts appear to have been too high.
Shift left to clear the jaw from the pot's upper edge, lower a few millimeters between its sides, then close in place.
Settle the centered pot grasp fully closed, then lift straight up slowly to verify retention before transporting or rotating it.
The pot again slipped from the jaws. Clear it and approach the upright alarm clock first; the figurine will need a different grasp.
Lower the open left jaws around the clock's sides with a small lateral centering correction, preserving its upright orientation.
Center the clock between the left jaws, descend slightly below its upper edge, and close fully in place before lifting.
Keep the clock grasp closed and lift vertically to verify retention while preserving its orientation.
The clock was not retained. Reopen and approach deeper with a more vertical, yaw-aligned grasp around its sides instead of its upper corners.
A jaw is contacting the clock's upper corner. Lift clear, correct the yaw in the opposite direction, and recenter before descending again.
Translate the open gripper rightward along the clock's sides to center it, then lower below the upper corners for a deeper grasp.
Clear the clock's corner, reduce the yaw mismatch, and approach its sides farther back and lower rather than pressing on the top.
Make a final millimeter-scale centering correction and close on the clock's side faces, allowing the grasp to settle before lifting.
Test the deeper clock grasp with a slow straight lift, holding the jaws closed and watching for object motion relative to the wrist.
The clock now follows the left gripper. Lift it high enough to clear the drawer before translating onto the top.
After the continuity stop, use smaller upward increments with forward motion and a gradual shallower wrist angle to carry the retained clock over the drawer.
Avoid further forward extension at the continuity boundary. Shift the held clock left with only small rise and a shallower wrist angle, replanning from the single executed step.
Carry the retained clock slowly above the drawer's front rim with a modest rise, using small increments to preserve elbow-up continuity.
Use a lower, smaller forward placement path after the continuity stop. Keep the clock held while checking clearance over the drawer rim.
The clock appears supported on the drawer top. Open the left jaws, allow it to settle, then withdraw backward without sweeping across it.
Leave the clock on the drawer and approach the fallen figurine's narrow stem, turning the left gripper so its jaws close across the stem rather than along it.
Center the open jaws across the figurine's narrow stem and lower to a side-contact height, avoiding the wider pot.
Shift the left jaws laterally onto the narrow cactus neck and close in place. The clock has fallen from the front edge and will need replacement farther onto the top.
The jaws appear to have closed above the narrow stem. Reopen and lower a small amount before closing around its sides.
Settle the neck grasp, then lift the figurine straight up slowly with the left gripper closed to verify retention.
The stem did not lift. Reopen, move the grasp slightly toward the middle of the neck, and descend below the previous empty grasp before closing again.
Allow the deeper stem grasp to close fully, then lift vertically at low speed to check whether the figurine follows.
The stem appears retained. Lift farther, move toward the stand, and begin slowly rotating the sideways figurine upright with the jaws kept closed.
Continue righting the retained figurine while carrying it rightward and slightly away from the drawer, keeping the left wrist on its own side.
Use smaller rotations with an added sideways tilt to avoid the wrist continuity boundary while carrying the held figurine toward the stand.
Reduce both translation and rotation increments substantially after the one-step continuity interruption; keep the figurine held throughout.
The figurine slipped during reorientation. Reverse the wrist rotation gradually and return toward it with open jaws, avoiding the singularity with small initial increments.
Replan with uniformly small wrist and translation increments after the continuity rejection, moving clear of the drawer toward the figurine's new lying orientation.
Use only the previously accepted small wrist-unwinding direction; omit the yaw and backward motion that caused the zero-step rejection.
Continue unwinding the left wrist in small combined increments while moving backward from the drawer, preparing a grasp across the figurine's new stem direction.
Move the open left gripper toward the front of the fallen figurine while gradually restoring a downward, left-right closing orientation.
Finish aligning the left gripper across the fallen stem and lower with the jaws open, preserving the continuous elbow-up configuration.
Center the left jaws on the narrow trunk between the pot and side branches, descend to its side faces, and close without lifting yet.
Settle the new trunk grasp, then lift vertically with the jaws closed before attempting further reorientation.
The trunk appears retained. Lift clear of the nearby clock, translate toward the stand, and begin righting the figurine with a gradual world-x rotation.
Continue slowly righting the retained figurine while carrying it toward the stand. Keep the left grasp closed and avoid the keyboard on the right.
Replan after the five-step interruption: lower and retract slightly to regain elbow-up margin while gently continuing to right the held figurine.
The figurine slipped during rotation. Reopen and reset to a vertical approach over its pot; prioritize a stable short transfer to the stand without further midair righting.
Use the wrist view to center the pot farther forward between the open jaws, then lower toward its side faces.
The downward target was not tracked, likely from drawer-side interference. Clear it backward and shift the wrist right while angling the open fingers left toward the pot.
Center the pot between the open jaws with a small rightward correction and descend to its side faces, then close and settle without rotating.
Test the centered pot grasp with a slow lift and short translation toward the stand, keeping its current orientation to reduce slipping.
